name: Rabicano
summary: White ticking that starts at the tail dock and the flank and works forward - a frosted, banded coon tail, a scatter of white hairs over the rear barrel and belly, and broken vertical rib bars on the strongest ones. How much shows varies from horse to horse and can be almost nothing, so a horse recorded as solid can throw a heavily ticked foal. Not classic roan: the tail tells them apart, and it lacks the large face and leg white of sabino patterns. Held here as a made-up dominant allele: it is thought dominant in some families, but that is not established. No gene, variant or DNA test is published. The best lead is a 2021 UC Davis dissertation (Esdaile): in 61 rabicano horses and 36 controls, a possible 1.7 Mb haplotype around KITLG on chromosome 28 was associated with it, its best marker (rs397240012, g.15967332G>A on EquCab3.0) in a skin enhancer about 160 kb upstream of KITLG; no coding variant tested matched the phenotype fully. KITLG is the signal KIT receives, but no KIT allele is known to cause rabicano. Seen in Quarter Horses, Arabians, Thoroughbreds, Warmbloods, Mangalarga and Criollo horses. No known effect on build, speed or the long hair.

phenotypes.name: Rabicano
phenotypes.description: White ticking from the tail dock and flank forward - a frosted, banded coon tail and a scatter of white hairs over the rear barrel and belly. How much shows varies enormously and can be almost nothing: a horse recorded as solid can carry it and throw a strongly ticked foal.

phenotypes.name: Strong rabicano
phenotypes.description: Two copies. The same pattern with its floor raised - a horse that never comes out entirely plain, often with broken vertical rib bars up the barrel and enough white to be mistaken for a roan until you look at its tail.
